Systems Software Engineer, Hardware Validation

About us:

Voyant Photonics builds silicon photonic chips that steer and switch light at high speed. They power next generation, chip-scale FMCW LiDAR for robotics and autonomy, and optical circuit switches (OCS) for AI data centers. Based in NYC, we’re a hands-on team designing, building, and deploying frontier hardware to solve problems that matter, from how machines see to how AI scales.

About the role

Our tech stack spans FPGA and ASIC logic, microcontroller firmware, Linux drivers and cross platform user-facing APIs, and every layer changes every week. We're hiring engineers, at more than one level, to keep them integrated, tested and releasable.

What Actually Matters

Code is cheaper to write than ever. Knowing what should be written, and what "done" means, is the job. We want someone with strong, well-reasoned opinions about how software should be organized and how test coverage should grow, who argues for them, and who changes their mind when the evidence says so.

Things we believe in as a team:

 - Fix it at the source. A bug gets fixed where it lives, even when that's someone else's code. The friction of working in each other's areas is worth it.

 - Live at the tip. Every repo tracks the latest of everything it depends on. Small, frequent bumps surface breaks while they're still cheap to fix.

 - Duplicated code is broken code. Two copies drift apart, and then one of them is wrong.

 - It doesn't work until someone else has run it on hardware. Your own simulation or bench is where you start, not where you're done.

Disagree with one? Tell us why when you apply.

What You'll Do

 - Own releases from commit to customer: build, verify, version and ship product bundles (FPGA bitstreams, firmware, drivers, APIs), including field updates, with release notes and runbooks people trust.

 - Grow our HIL CI to cover every subsystem, and bring each new product into it from its first bring-up board.

 - Track every bug CI finds to its root cause, whether that's Python, Rust, firmware, a Linux driver or FPGA logic, then fix it.

 - Take our products into the systems that use them: time sync, calibration, sensor fusion, and open-source ecosystems like OCP and ROS.

What We're Looking For

 - 2+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent depth from research, internships or serious personal projects. We'll scale scope to experience.

 - Strong Python, and comfort debugging languages you don't write every day.

 - Hands-on hardware experience: bring-up, reading schematics, and using lab instruments to tell a software bug from a board bug.

 - CI/CD experience, ideally against real hardware.

 - Proactive communicator who cares about documentation to support cross functional team members & customers.

Nice to Have

 - Rust, C++ or embedded C (we use STM32)

 - Linux device drivers, especially SPI and custom low-level interfaces

 - Reading System Verilog well enough to debug across the FPGA boundary

 - HIL rigs and lab automation (SCPI/VISA, self-hosted CI runners)

 - Timing and signal-integrity debug across SPI, I2C, UART, Ethernet and JTAG/SWD, plus board rework

 - Fiber optics and optical test equipment

 - Datacenter networking, PTP, point clouds or ROS 2

 - Supporting software that external customers depend on

What You'll Gain

 - Ownership of the release and test architecture for our products, from first bring-up to shipping: real decisions, not someone else's pipeline.

 - Close collaboration with hardware, optics, signal processing and perception engineers, and real influence over technical direction at an early-stage company.

 - A path toward customer-facing integration work, if that interests you.

Life at Voyant

We build frontier hardware & software from our lab and office in Midtown Manhattan, where optical tables, lab benches and electronics sit alongside traditional office space. Our work is hands-on and primarily in person, but we don’t run on a rigid 9-to-5. We partner with customers across time zones, so some calls start early or run late, and we adjust schedules around them. We run a high-trust, high-accountability environment: you’ll own meaningful work, move quickly and often wear more than one hat. Voyant provides catered lunch every day at HQ, and we’re a diverse group of food lovers from around the world who enjoy sharing food, culture and technical ideas around the lunch table.



Equal Opportunity Employer

Exa is an applied AI lab building a search engine unlike the world has ever seen. We build massive-scale infra to crawl the entire web, train state-of-the-art embedding models to process it, and design super high performant vector databases to retrieve over it. We now power search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot, and over 400,000 developers and have raised $350m from Lightspeed, Benchmark, and a16z.

Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you.

The Knowledge Platform team builds Exa's knowledge engine. We continuously synthesize information from across the web and beyond into one of the world's largest open-domain knowledge graphs, with hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims. The work has two halves: construction pipelines that decide what to trust, and retrieval engines that decide how best to search it. Our goal is to give agents answers to any factual question about the world with unprecedented precision and completeness.

In this role, you'll own the query engine that searches hundreds of billions of claims across a variety of retrieval backends, from a distributed graph database to vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial indexes.

This is greenfield work with a massive scope. No off-the-shelf system answers precise questions over hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims at agent speed, so you'll make foundational decisions, from storage layout and indexing across engines to the query language and the planner that routes work between them, that every query depends on.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own storage and indexing across backends: data layout, partitioning and indexes for graph, vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial retrieval, with bulk snapshot builds and live ingest that never take the system down.

 - Decide how best to search: cost-based planning from cardinality estimates that chooses, for each question, which backends to use, in what order and how to join their results, executed as traversals, retrievals, filters and aggregations in one plan.

 - Make it fast at scale: serve thousands of queries per second, profiling and cutting p50/p99 latency, memory and cost per query under high concurrent load, from on-disk layout to network fan-out.

 - Keep answers consistent while the data converges: the graph is fed by live updates and bulk snapshots at once and is eventually consistent by design, so you'll own what a query may see while it converges: consistent snapshot promotion, ordered application of live updates and stable pagination across versions.

 - Measure precision and completeness: end-to-end checks every deployment must pass, plus evals and metrics that show when a plan returns wrong results or misses ones it should have found.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've worked deep inside a distributed database, query engine, search engine or storage system.

 - Strong grasp of indexing, query planning and optimization, and storage formats.

 - Solid grasp of distributed systems fundamentals: consensus, replication, sharding and fault tolerance.

 - Strong in a systems language (Go, Rust or C++).

 - You profile before you optimize, and you've shipped measured latency wins in production.

 - You obsess over correctness, reliability and data quality as much as scale.


BONUS

 - Graph databases, or combining vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial retrieval

 - Compilers, query language design or cost-based optimizers


EXAMPLE PROJECTS

 - Build a system that retrieves and reasons over everything known about any company or person in the world, answering any factual question precisely and completely.

 - Answer precise multi-hop questions over hundreds of billions of claims at thousands of QPS with interactive latency.

 - Build a planner that picks the right mix of graph, vector, full-text and geospatial retrieval for any question, and proves it chose well.

 - Make new knowledge queryable seconds after it's synthesized, without ever serving an inconsistent result.


LOGISTICS

 - Location: This is an in-person opportunity in San Francisco.

 - Visas: We're happy to sponsor international candidates (e.g., STEM OPT, OPT, H1B, O1, E3). While we cannot guarantee your visa, we have historically been successful in sponsoring candidates from all over the world. If you receive an offer, our team will work hard to get you a visa.

 - Benefits: We offer premium healthcare benefits (medical, dental, vision), fertility benefits, 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents, and a monthly wellness stipend to all of our employees.
